content:
Here’s a practical **NCLEX to-do list** you can follow:

## 1. Confirm your eligibility
- Graduate or confirm expected graduation date
- Apply to your **state board of nursing**
- Complete any required background check/fingerprinting
- Send transcripts or school documents if required

## 2. Register for the NCLEX
- Register with **Pearson VUE**
- Pay the exam fee
- Wait for your **Authorization to Test (ATT)**
- Double-check your name matches your ID exactly

## 3. Schedule your exam
- Pick a test date
- Choose a testing center or confirm online testing options if available
- Schedule early so you get the date you want
- Put the exam date in your calendar

## 4. Gather study materials
- Choose **1 main question bank** and stick with it
- Get an NCLEX review book or notes
- Use the current **NCLEX test plan**
- Collect lab values, isolation precautions, and prioritization basics

## 5. Make a study plan
- Set a target number of study weeks
- Study **most days each week**
- Break content into categories:
  - Med-surg
  - Pharmacology
  - Maternity
  - Pediatrics
  - Psych
  - Fundamentals
  - Leadership/delegation
- Schedule practice questions daily

## 6. Focus on high-yield NCLEX topics
Make sure you can handle:
- **Prioritization**: who to see first
- **Safety**
- **Delegation and assignment**
- **Infection control/isolation precautions**
- **Pharmacology basics**
- **Fluid and electrolytes**
- **ABGs**
- **EKGs** basics if tested in your prep
- **Maternal/newborn emergencies**
- **Peds milestones and safety**
- **Psych therapeutic communication**

## 7. Practice NCLEX-style questions
- Do questions every day
- Read **all rationales**, even for correct answers
- Practice:
  - Multiple choice
  - SATA/case-based formats
  - Bow-tie, matrix, cloze, prioritization if included in your resources
- Track weak areas and review them weekly

## 8. Master test-taking strategies
- Ask: **What is the safest answer?**
- Ask: **Which patient is unstable?**
- Use **ABCs** when appropriate
- Think **acute before chronic**
- Think **unexpected vs expected**
- Choose **therapeutic communication**
- Avoid answers that delay action when action is needed
- Be careful with absolutes like “always” and “never”

## 9. Build endurance
- Take at least **2–4 full-length practice exams**
- Practice sitting for long periods
- Work on pacing and staying calm when unsure

## 10. Fix weak areas
- Review missed topics
- Redo difficult question sets
- Memorize critical labs and precautions
- Practice delegation:
  - RN vs LPN/LVN
  - UAP tasks
- Review common emergency interventions

## 11. Prepare for test week
- Stop cramming the night before
- Review quick notes only
- Confirm test center location and time
- Prepare your ID
- Set out clothes, snacks, directions
- Sleep well

## 12. Test day checklist
- Eat something light
- Arrive early
- Bring correct ID
- Use breaks if needed
- Don’t panic if the exam feels hard
- Focus on one question at a time

## 13. After the exam
- Follow your state board for results
- Check whether your state participates in quick results
- Avoid overanalyzing how many questions you got

---

## Simple weekly study template
- **Mon–Fri:** 75–150 questions + rationales
- **Daily:** 1 content review topic
- **Sat:** practice exam + review weak areas
- **Sun:** lighter review/rest

---

## Biggest priorities if you’re short on time
1. Do lots of questions  
2. Review rationales carefully  
3. Learn prioritization/safety/delegation  
4. Focus on weak areas  
5. Take practice exams  

If you want, I can also make you a **30-day NCLEX study plan** or a **high-yield NCLEX checklist**.
